chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali from Ma'mar, raising it, said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said in one of his sermons: 'The most superior deed is maintaining the dignity with the wealth'.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the most superior deed according to Imam Ali in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies 'preserving one's honor through wealth' as the supreme deed, emphasizing that financial stability is a primary means of safeguarding dignity (*ird*) from humiliation. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that material sufficiency is not merely for luxury but is a spiritual and social necessity to maintain modesty and independence in public life. The phrase underscores the ethical responsibility to use resources proactively to prevent the loss of status that often accompanies poverty.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ali, from Moama, raising it, said,
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said in one of his<sup>asws</sup> sermons: ‘The most superior deed is maintaining the dignity with the wealth’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Ali has narrated from Mu’ammar in a marfu‘ manner from ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following: “In one of his speeches, ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The best deed is protecting one’s dignity by means of wealth.’”
